utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, Mr. Court Deputy.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is Case Number IT-02-60-T, The Prosecutor versus Vidoje Blagojevic and Dragan Jokic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Before the cross-examination, are there any matters that the parties would like to bring to the attention of this Bench? Well, I have a scheduling issue to discuss with the Prosecution. Yesterday, we received that list of the potential witnesses in this case before the winter recess. And we have been told that like all the offices, everybody wants to clean their table before the winter recess, so this Tribunal will have a very busy schedule before the winter recess. And because of the problem of the courtroom, we have to cancel a hearing, a sitting, on the 15th of December. So my question is whether it's possible to move that witness designated for that day somewhere to the previous week, or is it possible for us to hear four witnesses in four days for the last week?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President. As you know, there's always a certain amount of tentativeness in this because we're not sure how long that first week of December will take. The witnesses that we have for that week of 15 December, one is a Dutch soldier who I believe is in Holland so he should be relatively simple to move around. The others are Bosnian Muslims, and none of them should be really very long. So I think we have a fair amount of flexibility there, and we will try to make the most of it, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Ms. Sinatra.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, this is not my witness but I'd like to address the Court on the cross-examination of Mr. Butler. Mr. Stojanovic will need a full two days of cross-examination for Mr. Butler, so I just wanted to make sure that the Court was aware that he will need that amount of time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I see. Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, I was asked whether I could finish today. I informed Ms. Sinatra that I was not going to be able to do, nor would I rush the cross-examination for the sake of someone else's scheduling. We lost a session yesterday. And by my estimation, I will need the full day on Monday. And that is streamlining it, and I know it seems like a lot of time, but when we keep in mind the gentleman has generated four reports, testified for five days, testified in the Krstic case, and we have all these other documents that were introduced by the Prosecution, in my normal practice I would be cross-examining the gentleman for about three weeks. Very easily. I know it seems odd, but I would. So I have streamlined it, and I think we're making progress. But I can assure you, Your Honours, that I will not be able to finish today. But I promise to finish on Monday, but I will need the full day on Monday. And I think that would also assist Mr. Stojanovic in not having to break his cross. I understand he's got two days, and then, of course, there would be -- I would suspect there might be some redirect and questions from the Bench which probably -- I don't know if it will take two full days, but I think probably the rest of the week. And I don't know where that leaves Mr. Manning, but according to Mr. McCloskey, Mr. Manning would not be coming on. If we could not fit him in, he would be brought back at a latter point. Again, I would stress that this witness is an important witness to this entire case. When we consider that life sentences are being sought, at least for one of the accused, this is not the kind of witness that we should try to expedite the cross in order to meet some scheduling problems that we may have in the future. Lastly, with respect to the witnesses that were mentioned by you, Mr. President, of the last week, I concur with Mr. McCloskey. I don't foresee very much cross, if any, at least on our part. And I think it's not possible, but probable in all likelihood that we can accommodate the scheduling of that. And also, I'm fully willing to go full days. I don't know about the rest, but I'm fully, you know -- if we have the facilities available.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, thank you very much for your information. And originally, we planned to finish the testimony of this witness by next Tuesday. But now, it seems to me that is not possible. So I believe that we have to discuss with the Registrar about the further arrangements of this hearing. But I want to remind the parties that as I said before, that during the end of the year, we have a very, very tight scheduling in this Tribunal. It seems to me that there's so many hearings and it's very difficult to get a courtroom for extra time sitting. Well, let us discuss it with the Registrar during the break to see if there's any further arrangements for that. Yes, Ms. Sinatra.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Of course, Your Honour, we are offering to accept Dean Manning under 94 bis (D) or (C). I think that would save the Court's time. And documents, we have no problems with the admission of his forensic reports, if the Court would reconsider that offer. Also, on the last week, there is only one witness that I know is fairly important to the Defence of Mr. Jokic, and that's another intercept witness. The last witness will need to be cross-examined. I don't know at what length until we hear his direct testimony, but he will need to be cross-examined. And then of course the week of December 1st are the most important witnesses, the Zvornik Brigade engineering company soldiers who will be here. So I'm not sure that those are going to be short witnesses, Your Honour. I just wanted the Court to be prepared that these are very important witnesses to Mr. Jokic's Defence. And we will probably in all likelihood in each one of those listed, they're protected witnesses, we will need a full day for direct and cross-examination of those witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your good suggestion. But concerning with Mr. Dean Manning's testimony, I believe this Trial Chamber has made a decision already. And as far as I understand, some of the December 1st week witnesses are the 92 bis live witness which means that the direct examination won't take much long time, and I will give you enough time to cross-examine those witnesses. Well, having said that, let's start the cross-examination. Mr. Karnavas. By the way, we received a new list every day. It seems that you are very diligent to furnish us with those new lists. And it really keeps growing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, I guess we shouldn't be deceived by appearances, Your Honour. Just because the list grows doesn't mean that the cross-examination is growing. Good morning, Mr. President, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And good morning, Mr. Butler.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, I would like to pick up from where we left off yesterday. If we could go to the question and answer, and I have a clean copy of yesterday's transcript. So if we could just look at the -- I'll hand it to you and you can flip to page 70. It's the question -- you can just look at the question, and I'll paraphrase it. Page 70. It's at the bottom, line 23. I basically ask when all three of the -- are in the building, that is the Main Staff, the Drina Corps, and the commander of the Bratunac Brigade, who is actually exercising command and control? And you gave us an answer, and I think it would be worth maybe if you could read that answer again, and then we can discuss that. If you want to read it aloud.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can put it on the ELMO, also.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You can put it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It will be page 71.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And it's line 2.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Starting on line 2. And the answer is: "It depends on what echelon formation forces that we're talking about. The argument can be made that wherever General Mladic is, he exercises command and control. And as the commander of an army, that is in a broad sense exactly what happens. However in the more stratified environment or military environment, commanders are going to exercise command and control generally within their competencies of command. "So while certainly there are going -- there are going to be instances where General Mladic will give orders to officers that may be one or two echelons below him. The fact that General Mladic is in command and in control in Bratunac doesn't mean that suddenly General Zivanovic isn't. And when General Zivanovic is in command and control ..."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Will the speaker please slow down when reading?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: ... It doesn't mean that Colonel Blagojevic isn't. It's no absolute in this issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay, so I take it what you're saying is that it all depends on the circumstances?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say less on the circumstances. There's actually, going back over the former JNA doctrine, there's actually a better term of art to use which is the one that they use which is considered to be first instance superiority, second instance superiority, and third instance, and it continues up. And it reflects the fact that while in the model that they use, a company commander may be the first instance superior, the battalion commander is the second instance superior, the brigade commander up. So it's not necessarily situation-dependant. The military situation -- or the military organisation tries to follow within the confines of how it's organised. There will be instances, obviously, where a superior commander can and does give orders to soldiers one or two echelons below. But by and large, the system is designed is that the orders will be properly transmitted within the organisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. That's under optimal conditions. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The system is designed to operate in a wartime environment, and it is generally recognised that in a wartime environment it's not optimal conditions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, that's what -- well, what I meant was -- well, the rules are designed to meet those needs when you are in a wartime situation, are they not?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, just breaking down your answer before I go on to my next set of questions, you say "within the more stratified environment or military environment." Is that what we had on the ground over there as General Mladic was ordering soldiers, not officers one or two echelons below him, but soldiers on what to do?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I used the phrase "stratified military environment," I use it to compare the fact that particularly to people without military backgrounds, some of the organisational idiosyncrasies that occur in a military, that people tend to transmit over to civilian apparatuses. Military organisations are designed to operate in a regimented and stratified manner and don't necessarily show the same flexibility or the same ability of a superior to task subordinates as common as civilian structures or organisations, like a business, for example.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. But was that happening on the ground during those days when Mladic was there?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is evidence that Mladic was giving orders to individual officers and soldiers, so yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: In fact, we had testimony in one instance where apparently General Mladic, in order to motivate a lieutenant colonel from the security -- the assistant commander of the security of the Drina Corps, he was even kicked in the rear end in front of other soldiers. Is that within the stratified environment or military environment? Is that the sort of conduct you would expect of the highest commander?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly it is a poor leadership trait.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, getting back -- let's get back to my initial question. Who's in command at those headquarters? You have Mladic over is there, and he certainly has some of his staff, does he not?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that depending on the day, there are between two and four people from the Main Staff who are with Mladic. I'm not counting for sake of staff the two Main Staff individuals who were doing filming. So I'm generally -- between two and four of Main Staff officers depending on whether it was the 12th or the 13th.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And one of those that you might be referring to is Colonel Jankovic. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And in fact, at least if we can accept Mr. Nikolic's testimony on this particular issue, he has testified that Colonel Jankovic appeared at the Bratunac Brigade headquarters and took office in his office as, I believe, early as July 8th, 1995. Are you aware of that information?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am aware of the information. Again, like I said, my evidence is based on the video where we have him there on the 11th. He could have arrived earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Aside from General Mladic, we have General Zivanovic who, in those days, was still the commander, do we not?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And with him is his chief of staff. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And so you have the number one and the number two of the Drina Corps in the Bratunac area, in the Bratunac headquarters, on the 11th and 12th, and perhaps sometimes on the 13th as well, do we not?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, generally speaking.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And aside from those two, were there others from the Drina Corps staff?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were a number of officers from the Drina Corps staff, probably upwards of ten.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And how many of those officers were assistant commanders?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: At various times, I believe all three of the assistant commanders of the Drina Corps were present.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And who were they, if you could tell us?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would be Colonel Cerovic who would be the assistant commander of morale, legal, and religious affairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Lieutenant Colonel Popovic, the assistant commander for security.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: And Colonel Acamovic who is the assistant commander for rear services.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Where does Kosoric fit into this?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Kosoric is the chief of intelligence, so he falls into the operative staff. He is not an assistant commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, did Acamovic play a role during these days?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, it is my understanding that on a number of occasions, members of DutchBat talked to him with respect to issues of fuel and transportation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And he would be the logical person because that would fall within his branch, rear services. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, we touched on the meeting -- we touched on that meeting, a little bit, the first one. And I think we agreed that on that meeting, General Mladic was in command and control. What about the second meeting when the discussions are going on as to what will happen with all of the people that have gathered in Potocari? Who is in command and in control at that time?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: General Mladic certainly dictated that meeting. I don't believe any other VRS officer spoke.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And at the conclusion of that particular meeting, were you able to make some sort of a conclusion as to what General Mladic had represented to those with whom he was meeting?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Insomuch as General Mladic he directed that the transportation was going to begin at a certain time, yes, sir. I mean, that was fairly evident from the video.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, it seems to me from the second meeting, there was a request or some discussion with the UN as to whether the UN would be able to facilitate the transfer of those who wished to leave. But for logistical purposes, they were unable to do so. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And now we have the third meeting. The third meeting is on the morning of the 12th. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that would be 1000 hours on 12 July.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And so before we get to the third meeting, would not one expect that in light of the discussions from the second meeting, that some preparations would have begun to put forward the plan for the evacuation of those who wished to leave Potocari?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, and in fact I believe the documentary evidence that we have indicates that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. But that would be a natural event. One would expect that under the circumstances, would they not?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Particularly given that it was the summer. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It had been hot in those days. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The DutchBat had very little food and water to provide for those who had gathered in Potocari. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly the number of people vastly outstripped their own capacity to do anything with them, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And if it was not deemed a humanitarian crisis, one was looming at least not far behind?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And so on the 12th of the morning, we have the third meeting. And again, I believe you would conclude that Mladic was in command and in control. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, again he dictated all of the events.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, he not only dictated what the terms, if I could put it that way, the terms to those with whom he was meeting, but would it be fair to say that he also dictated the orders of which he wished to have his lower echelon carry out?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, before we get to that, there are some -- let's talk about Potocari. We do see General Mladic going to Potocari on the 12th, do we not?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I believe there is video evidence of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now I think we can all agree that in part, that was a propaganda event. Mladic being seen there as the general who had finally been able to capture Srebrenica. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. I mean, obviously he was mugging for the cameras.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And with him one would expect to find military police from the Bratunac Brigade as his security and as the rules required for the Bratunac Brigade to provide such security for a top echelon such as General Mladic. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. I mean, in fact, you see not only that, you see General Mladic's own personal security, his close-in security detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Who is in command and who is in control of the people that have gathered in Potocari on the 12th?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say overall responsibility rests with General Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And of course, again, he's going to issue tasks to the lower echelon to carry out his particular orders. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. That's an application of the chain of command.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And at that point in time, at that point in time, General Mladic had, in fact, had he not, openly pronounced that it would be a safe evacuation?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure whether that was his pronouncement or whether that was General Krstic's on the video because he made the same type of announcement. There may be a second one from Mladic I'm unaware of.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, let's backtrack. In the past, during those meetings, he had made such pronouncements, had he not?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that he did effectively say that the people would be given a choice. I'm not sure if issue of safety came up, but I assume there would be safe conduct on that one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The implication being that they would be able to leave, those who wished to leave. He was not going to block them. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, and he indicated that the disarming process also had to occur.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. He had some conditions on that.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And I take it those listening to him at the time would come away with some conclusion, would they not?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection. Which time? He talks a lot those days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: General Mladic is making --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I understand that, you know, Mr. Karnavas is asking the question according to that logic. But, Mr. Karnavas, if you could be more specific, I believe that it would be helpful.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I will, Your Honour. I will.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: When General Mladic was openly stating that nothing would happen or that they would be free to go, one who was listening would walk away with the conclusion that General Mladic was, in essence, guaranteeing the safe evacuation of these people, would they not?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I think that's a fair assumption.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, General Mladic doesn't stick around from the 11th all the way to the 15th, 16th, 17th in Bratunac. He comes and he goes, correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: My understanding is that he was in and around the Bratunac area until late afternoon 13 July. And again, his whereabouts after that, apparently there are three different versions of that floating around. Like I said, I don't know that he comes back at a point in time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. But we do see him around the vicinity where certain activity is occurring, I think as late as the 15th, do we not?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, my understanding is that the best evidence is that on 15 July, General Mladic is in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: He is meeting with the contact group, and they would presumably be in a position to know if he wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. After General Mladic leaves, I take it General Zivanovic, up until the time that he's replaced, he's the next in line as far as who is in command and who is in control. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, again, your point, Mr. Karnavas, is the fact that General Mladic is there as the commander on the ground does not mean that de facto General Zivanovic is somehow not the Drina Corps commander and is not himself exercising command and control within his own competencies.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not an either/or situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Let me give you an example. General Mladic gives an order that he wants the rear services of the Drina Corps to provide for the transfer of those who have gathered in Potocari, women and children, let's say, we'll stick with that, to the safe areas. Okay? Now, that order gets passed down directly to Zivanovic, so Zivanovic has to act on it, does he not?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Then let's say Zivanovic then goes to his rear services assistant commander, that would be Acamovic, who we know was there, and says "make this happen." Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: He would essentially give the commander the guidance to do that. Hopefully it would be more than just "make this happen." But depending on how specific General Mladic's guidance was, it could be that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, were there in Bratunac, in the Bratunac headquarters, you've already indicated that's the forward command post of the Drina Corps at that point in time. Now, if Acamovic were to then go to the rear services, directly to the rear services of the Bratunac Brigade and give an order, would that not -- would that order not be an extension of the order given by General Mladic?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. And in fact, what you've just described is almost the proper working of the chain of command.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Because they don't need -- they don't need to go to the commander of the Bratunac Brigade in that instance because of the concept of functional relationships. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: As long as the order would not impact other broader areas. And again, the key person in this part of the argument would be the Bratunac Brigade chief of rear services, Major Trisic, who would be the one to recognise that whether this is an order in that functional relationship which he could implement on his own, or whether this is something that would have to go back through his commander because it would require assets and resources outside of his scope. So that's -- the key person in that would be, then, Major Trisic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, to make it clear to everyone here, let's go to the rules, because I think the rules give us some guidance, but I think we are on the same wavelength on this one. If we could turn to D84, which is a segment from the Prosecution's evidence P394. It's the manual for the work of commands and staff. It's a draft 1983. You referred to it, Mr. Butler, and I'm sure you have studied it. I just made a little excerpt. If you feel more comfortable with your entire volume --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which page are you referring to, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We're going to go step by step. Step by step.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Do you recognise this document, sir?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And in fact, you've made references to this document which is titled "manual for the work of commands and staff." Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if we turn to the first page, it's page 5, but actually it's the -- if we look at the title of it, it's just an introductory page. And we look at the second paragraph, and I'll just read it. It's very short. It says: "The manual is to be used in the work of commands and staffs, institutions for all command and staff operations in the training of commanding officers, commands, and staffs and units and in the education process in the military schools." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And basically this manual is the manual on how to command. Correct? It's a draft at this point, but in essence, I think that's all we have and that's what you have been making references to. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: More than just how to command; it explains in detail the command and staff relationships with each other. And again, there are significant language with what you have called, you know, the proper term, functional relationships between higher and lower staffs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. So that's what I want to go through because I think we need a very clear record on this. Although again, I think we're on the same wavelength. If we turn to the next page, it would be page 13. And as you could see, this is chapter 1. It's the chapter on functions of control and their interdependence. And we can go down to paragraph 3, we see that it's about -- this paragraph deals with the issue of control: Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And you've read this, have you not?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Before we get to it, it makes sense, you having a military background, even though you come from a different military structure, when you read these guidelines, it make sense as -- these rules, don't they?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. They very much dovetail with what I would call universal dictates among militaries.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. So we have: "Control is a function" -- I'll just read it, paragraph 3. And I'm referring to again, for the record, D84. "Control is a function (activity) of the organisation of the armed forces whose aim is to direct individuals, organisational units, and armed forces as a whole in the execution of the goals and tasks that have been set." Now, I'm going to skip the rest and go to the next portion of the same paragraph. It says: "Control in the armed forces is essentially characterised by two forms: Control as a social relationship and control as a work process of commanding officers and commands/staffs and other organs." You agree with that, do you not?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And what exactly does that say in plain language?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In plain language, the control as a social relationship is a, I believe what they described is that's a face-to-face orders process. The control as a work process of commanding officers and commands and staffs and other organs is the military process by which the complex functions of an army work through a command and his staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. In fact, if you went one paragraph further down within paragraph 3, it says: "Control as a social relationship expresses the class essence of the relationship between the superior and his subordinate manifesting..." And it goes on and on. Now if we go to number 4, paragraph number 4, it says: "Three kinds of relationships are essentially manifested in the control system in the armed forces: One, command relationship; two, functional relationship; and three, staff relationship." And if we turn to the next page, it then goes on and it says on paragraph 5: "The command relationship is based on the principles of unity, unity of command and subordination; it is defined in the relationship between the superior and his subordinate." So now I think this is the universal principle that we have been talking about that should, and in all likelihood does, exist in every organised army. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If you go further down in the next paragraph, but still within number 5, it says, and I'm reading from the second line: "It is an obligation to execute the tasks set by one's superior or competent officers and organs in an accurate and proper manner and to act in accordance with the military regulations in their execution." You would agree with me. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And in fact, they even say, if you don't do it - within that same paragraph - you have disorganisation?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: In fact, we saw a little bit of disorganisation after the fall of Srebrenica as a result of some of General Mladic's -- how shall I say it -- unorthodox behaviour in command?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would disagree with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, it was for me an excellent example of where a commander was making a decision and where his subordinates believe that it was the incorrect decision and talked to him about it, and he modified his order.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm not talking about just that one. I'm talking in general, where he's fading in and he's fading out of the picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, objection.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I disagree.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We need some specificity. That's vague.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The witness seemed to understand me, Your Honour, and I'm sure Mr. McCloskey does as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, I think that request is legitimate. You have to lay some specific grounds for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We have Colonel Beara coming into the picture at some point, do we not?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe he comes into the picture as early as -- or at least as early as I see him is approximately 1000 hours on 13 July.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And he's from the Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: At the same time you have staff officers of the Drina Corps around there. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, going to the functional relationships, it says: "Functional relationships are established by the organs of the command staff or other commanding officers in order for the tasks to be executed in a coordinated manner."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could you please slow down for the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If we skip further down, it says: "Functional relationships are established by the organs of the command/staff and other organs participating in the execution of the task. The task in its entirety and the set of activities determine the level of functional connections. Functional relationships are the basis for the organisation of cooperation and collaboration and for coordination in the course of the execution of missions." Now, in order to understand that, let's go down to staff relationships and see how these two interrelate and how this principle fits within the context in which we first raised it with respect to the rear services back on July 12th, 1995. It says here: "Staff relationship is the established manner in which work is carried out and relationships formed within the command, manifesting the relationship between the decision-maker" and then it goes on, presidency, committee, commander, chief, director, et cetera, "and other organs which carry out analyses necessary for the decision-making or monitor and assess the situation in the course of the execution of the task." Now, if we go to the very last paragraph within paragraph number 7, it says: "Staff relationships between command organs and staffs at a higher and lower organisational level are, in fact, functional relationships governed by the principle of obligatory action in accordance with the requests of the staff organ of the superior command for the purpose of implementing the decision made by the superior commander." Now, when we look at that and we go back to where we started, at my example, Acamovic, who is the assistant commander of the rear services, receives his order from his commander, General Zivanovic. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, he can then, because he is the assistant commander of the rear services, he can go to a lower level within the same branch, the same organ, call it what you will, that is, the rear services, and go directly there and give an order as long as it is within the confines of the order given to Acamovic by Zivanovic. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that's a proper explanation of a functional relationship.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And in doing so, Acamovic can bypass completely the commander of the Bratunac Brigade as long as, with the caveat that you injected, the order that is given to the assistant commander of rear services of the Bratunac Brigade is within the confines of the general order given to him by his superior?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, I would disagree with the bypass.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, do they need to give him -- do they need his authorisation?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: He needs to be aware as the commander. And authorisation depending on the task and functions is situation-dependant. They may. The thing to remember in this programme is that the brigade staff exists for the benefit of the brigade commander. The brigade staff or the lower staff is not a subordinate organ of a higher staff. So there is no divorcing that process.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Do you know what a backslider is, Mr. Butler? Someone who goes forward and then slides back. And I think that's what you've just done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection, we're back to silly barbs. That's not necessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, do not make any argument with the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm not arguing, Your Honour. I'm merely demonstrating that the gentleman before knowing where I was going committed himself to a position. Now he's sliding back because his colleague there -- he wants to advocate the Prosecution's case because he is a member of the Prosecution. That's what I'm demonstrating.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Now, whether or not the witness slides back, and we could see it from the transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I agree, Your Honour. I apologise. I will continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Nothing, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Let's be clear, Mr. Karnavas, what I'm doing --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm entitled to ask the questions --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understand, and I want to answer them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Let the witness finish his answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I haven't posed a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I think the witness wants to say something.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: In that case.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What I am describing, what I have described, and what I continue describing are the proper allocations of the exercise of command and control. I am not prepared to ascribe to a theory that under a proper reading of the JNA rules and regulations that a brigade commander or a corps commander staff can effectively be hijacked by a superior. I expect if you have a military expert who will subscribe to that, you will bring him up. But that is not a proper, and it is not what is envisioned in the JNA rules and regulations. And if you have a military expert who will say differently, I would like to hear that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Mr. Butler, Mr. Butler, I wasn't going to get there at this point. But you have been hired and you have been getting paid by the Prosecution for the last five to six years, have you not?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is incorrect, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, you were initially seconded to work for the Prosecution, getting paid by the United States government. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And then at some point you became an employee of the Prosecution. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So your bread and butter was being earned by being a member of the Prosecution team. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was where I was paid from for the last two years, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And you've already indicated that you're not independent. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And would it not be fair to conclude, to use your own logic, that after putting in so much work into this particular case and being a member of the Prosecution team, being a member of the team where you're strategising as to what evidence will be included in your report and not, and what will be said here in Court or not, and what documents will be introduced or not, is it not fair to conclude, sir, that you are not just here as an analyst, but you also have been an investigator, an interrogator, and also an advocate? Isn't that a fair conclusion for some of us to draw?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, you may choose to draw that conclusion. However, as I will remind you and everyone in the Court for that matter, as a retired professional military officer, I have more in common with the accused than I do with anyone else in this Court. And as such, as a basis of my analysis, as a basis of my looking at the documents, I have tried to do so in a conservative and fair manner because I understand intrinsically the issues with respect to the challenges that military commanders face, they face in combat situations, and the hard decisions they have to make on a daily basis. And that ultimately, they may have to answer for those decisions in an environment like this. And one day perhaps even my own country and my own fellow officers may have to do the same thing. So as a matter of my own personal philosophy, I don't believe in railroading military officers knowing that if that's going to be the path, then it may be that same track that runs over some of my own fellow officers, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, getting back to functional relationships, one of the reasons you have a functional relationship, is it not, is that one organ from the higher level can implement an order directly by going through to the lower level of the same organ? Isn't that one of the reasons for the existence of this functional relationship?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, the functional relationship exists so you have the most effective means of transmitting the orders of the superior through the subordinate for execution.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And there may be instances also where you have the commander, and maybe the chief of staff, as we had in this case at one point in time, when they're not in their headquarters, and a decision needs to be executed, carried out. And so one organ can go directly down to its sister organ below. And as long as what they are asking the lower organ to do is within the confines of the order that was given by the higher echelon, that can be done without getting authorisation from the commander. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, if it's within those competencies, they would not be normally required to get authorisation from the commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And in fact, there is nothing in here, is there, sir, that says that Acamovic had to get authorisation? That's the key phrase, authorisation from the commander of the Bratunac Brigade before he could go to the assistant commander of rear services of the Bratunac Brigade and task him to carry out orders which he had been given, that is, Acamovic had been given, from General Zivanovic which he had been given from Mladic?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, given the hypothetical here, again, it would go back to what the scope of the orders were.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Was the scope of the order given to Trisic, the assistant commander for rear services, by Acamovic, the assistant commander of the Drina Corps within the scope of what Acamovic had been tasked by General Zivanovic?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I don't know. I mean we're talking about hypothetical. I don't know what orders Colonel Acamovic gave to Major Trisic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, you do know, do you not, what Major Trisic was engaged in. Correct? At least some of them.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we go back to Major Trisic's interview, he was engaged in at one step the process of bringing foodstuff from the military bakery at Bratunac to Potocari --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Let me stop you there. We'll go step by step. Now, under the circumstances, was that not within the order -- the scope of the order given to Acamovic?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: My understanding from the interview, and it has been about a month since I've read this, he said that the order was given by his commander. I could be wrong, but...

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, is that, Mr. Butler --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand your question in this regard because I'm still back to --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You're here as the expert. You're here telling us you've analysed all these documents, and I'm trying to ask you, with Major Trisic giving bread and providing water, providing humanitarian aid, what in that is inconsistent with the orders that were given from the higher-up that trickled down all the way to him?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I'm going to object and ask that the counsel not interrupt the witness in the middle of his explanation, and I don't think there's a need to raise his voice either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, of course the counsel should not raise his voice in any situation. But the witness said that he did not understand the question, so Mr. Karnavas just gave an explanation. You are too soon. You have to wait until the witness finishes his answer so you can identify the specific problems of this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Butler, now, do you understand the question by the counsel?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir. But I guess what I don't understand, and maybe -- like I said, it has been a while since I read this interview, I don't understand the orders that are being attributed to the assistant commander for logistics, Acamovic in this instance.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Let me rephrase.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's where -- I don't doubt it. I just don't know it at this point.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you know what, if any, orders Acamovic was given?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: We have not been able to interview him, so I'm not sure what orders that he was given.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you know what --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not recalling that General Krstic mentioned that as a component of his. He may have, but I just don't recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Was -- were you unable to get a hold of Mr. Acamovic? Is that it? You could not locate him, or was it that it wasn't of any interest?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. I believe he was summonsed, but I don't know that the summons was able to be served or whatever. But I know that there was, in fact, interest.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You saw -- you are aware of some of his activities during the 12th and the 13th, are you not?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Are there any orders that go to Trisic, either oral or in writing, with respect to some of those activities?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 12th, we have the written order that presumably involved Trisic, the order from the Drina Corps to the Bratunac Brigade, for the assembly of buses from the various brigades. And of course, that went to all the Drina Corps Brigades. And that is a function that I would conclude that Major Trisic would be significantly involved in.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And what was the purpose for that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The purpose of the military order from the Drina Corps was to have all of the brigades assemble their buses, or the ones that they had directly with them, and have them sent to the Bratunac stadium by 1630, presumably those were going to be the vehicles that would be used to move the Muslim population from Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: How many of those buses did the Bratunac Brigade have that were functioning?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the answer to that. We did not get rear-service records from the Bratunac Brigade that details those.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And if you look at it in the greater context, as you would put it, of what General Mladic had told every -- had been saying and what was happening at the time, is there anything improper with Trisic complying with that order, if he did so comply?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Within the greater scheme of what was happening, his compliance would be expected.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: His compliance would be expected, but I'm saying was there anything sinister or nefarious about that? There's a humanitarian crisis, Mladic has indicated that the people will be able to leave. He's already provided or is providing bread and water. And now he's being tasked to assemble buses so that this transfer can occur, so the people can get out of the heat and go to a place or area where certainly their safety is going to be much better. So is there anything sinister or nefarious about carrying out this particular order if, indeed, he did carry it out?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. With this respect, I mean, the order is -- there's nothing wrong with it at face value.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. When you say "at face value," are you suggesting that at this point Mladic had informed Trisic of what his intent was going to be, if he did have an intent at that time?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. That's exactly what I mean, is that while I believe Mladic had an intent, from the face of that order, certainly Major Trisic would be unaware of that intent and would follow that order because at face value it's fully lawful. I mean, it's not a problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And in fact, do we not have some intercept conversations, and I believe there is even one document - we might get to it, depending on how we're doing on time - but we have one document that was generated by General Zivanovic which indicate that they don't know the whereabouts -- they don't know where the people are going to be taken to. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that -- I understand what you're saying. Again, I'm also unclear whether it's an intercept or a document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, let me see if I can --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I agree that at least in one instance, there was some question as to where the people would be taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, let me -- since we're on the topic on what people knew and what they did, if I could show you what has been marked as P434 for identification purposes.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've got it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Sorry for that. We see, do we not, sir, I believe you even commented about this because there is this little exchange between you and the Prosecution as to how to analyse intercepts and other information, the synthesis process. Here, we see it says -- first of all, this is from General Zivanovic, is it not?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It's dated 12 July 1995. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It looks like it was generated on or about 10.00. It says "processed at 1020 hours." Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. It was delivered at 1020, so this is the actual outbound signed one, so it would be in this particular instance, it would have been drafted at the Drina Corps headquarters to be sent out at 1020.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Was this drafted at the Drina Corps headquarters, or was it drafted at the Bratunac Brigade headquarters which was the forward command post at the time of the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Given the fact that it has a Drina Corps stamp, and this larger stamp is consistent with the documents that have come out of the headquarters of the Drina Corps as opposed to the documents we see in the Bratunac Brigade where it is just a handwritten notation, I believe this document was, in fact, drafted and signed at the Drina Corps headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And at this point, General Zivanovic is stating, and I'm reading from the first -- it will be the second sentence of the first paragraph. "Their final destination is unknown to us for the moment." Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, taken at face value, it would appear, would it not, that the commander of the Drina Corps at this point in time did not know the destination. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And I understand that General Zivanovic has not been indicted, although he has been questioned.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: He has been interviewed on a number of occasions. And to my knowledge, he has not been indicted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Judge, whether anyone has been indicted or not is really not relevant and it's not an appropriate question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It would be an appropriate question at this point in time, Your Honour, because at this point in time, 12 July, General Zivanovic is still the commander. And so if crimes were committed at that point in time, and he's the Drina Corps commander, it would stand to reason that he would be indicted for those crimes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, I think, you know, you have to remember the rule in the rules of procedure that this Tribunal has the power to issue a sealed indictment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I understand that, Your Honour. I totally understand that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: So if this issue is not directly related to your case, I hope you could move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I would just add, Your Honour, that it's clearly a well-known established fact that Mr. Karnavas would agree that an indictment itself is not evidence, and that, as he knows, the Prosecution does not indict all those that may have been guilty in the Tribunal. And so to try to draw an inference whether or not someone is guilty because whether or not they have been indicted is not a proper inference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'll move on, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: It's time for the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We'll resume at quarter to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Mr. Butler, we were speaking about General Zivanovic, and at least if we are to take this document that we spoke of, Prosecution Evidence 434, it would appear that he, the commander of the Drina Corps at that point in time, did not know the destination of the folks that were about to be transported out of Potocari. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But from this order, we also see that he's aware that there will be a need to make the necessary arrangements, logistic arrangements, for that transportation to occur. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. I mean he's specifying that the Main Staff needs to provide additional fuel resources.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And it would appear, would it not, that he, as the commander, of the Drina Corps, particularly since Potocari at this point in time would fall within the zone of responsibility as it's designated in the rules, that it would be up to him to ensure that General Mladic's order that the people be transported out be carried out?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, he would retain overall responsibility for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And I take it if General Zivanovic did not know the final destination, we can conclude that in all likelihood the commander -- the assistant commander of the rear services, Acamovic, also did not know the destination. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would disagree with that because as we note, at the time General Zivanovic is writing this, he is in Vlasenica. Colonel Acamovic as well as a number of other Drina Corps officers are at that same morning in Bratunac. And because of the proximity between them and General Mladic, they may well be aware of what the final destination is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Don't you think they would have communicated that to their commander?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would be something that I expect that they would do, and I don't know that it didn't occur at a point in time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But I'm talking about at this point in time, not some other point in time. At this point in time, you seem to be implying, albeit with some qualifications, that Acamovic, the deputy commander of rear services, would have known of the final destination while his commander, who is making this very urgent request, is totally unaware?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. When I'm going back to your question, was that just because General Zivanovic does not know at the time, because there is a physical separation between them, I can't make the same conclusion that Colonel Acamovic does not know at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. So here we have an instance -- we have an example where a commander is not necessarily aware of a circumstance. Correct? Even though they can easily reach each other through communication means. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And even though we have this superior -- the superior/inferior or superior/officer relationship. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. So -- and we have a very important situation on the ground. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, as you said, a developing humanitarian crisis. Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. And I just wanted to point out that here is an example where the commander is making a request, and you're telling us that in spite of his position, in spite of the situation on the ground, and though one would expect him to know the final destination, he in all likelihood if we are to accept this at face value does not know, while at the same time his assistant commander would have more information. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. What I'm saying is that as this document is drafted, General Zivanovic does not indicate and does not know presumably what the final destination is. I don't know when this document was drafted. We do know when it was sent out. But again, I don't know and I can't make a conclusion as to whether Colonel Acamovic knew more or less at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Would you take General Zivanovic's word at face value, based on this document, that is, that he did not know?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, at the time this was drafted I believe that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, we have another document, and that is -- I believe it's P191. This is an intercept. You have it? If not, I have it handy for you.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have it, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And you can put it on the ELMO. And on this document, there seems to be an exchange. You're aware of this document, are you not?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And in fact, you testified regarding this particular document. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now this conversation takes place at approximately 1240 hours. And I believe it's -- we're still on July 12th. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. So this would have been at least two hours-plus after the very urgent request sent by General Zivanovic. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, it seems that X is from Panorama. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That's the Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And do we know where Y is? Do we know --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm assuming that from the internal part of the conversation from Y that it is Bratunac. It doesn't compromise its own, but the fact that it's noting some of the events, and "this morning, we organised it from here," I'm concluding that Y is in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Fair enough. And what can we glean from this? In fact, why don't you read it so we can then deconstruct it.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the beginning, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: From the beginning. It's a short one.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Y states: "We are starting the evacuation of those who want to go to Kladanj." X says: "Okay." Y says: "Pass it on. Just let/objects missing/provide transportation. There's just three dots for X. And Y says: "And reinforce... With trucks and buses, and a water tank should be sent to give them water and food. This morning, we organised it here. We'll give them everything. I talked with them, and we'll accept all of the civilians who want to and they can stay. Those who don't want to can choose where they'll go." X is: "..." Then Y: "... See you, bye."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: From this conversation, it would appear, would it not, that Y is under the impression that those who want to stay can stay, and those who want to leave can leave. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And in fact, it shows here that at least Y, assuming Y is at the Bratunac Brigade, is under the impression that the trucks that are heading over there and the food that's going there is for the purposes of to assist the folks that have gathered in Potocari. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And so the impression that Y would get, would he not, or she, depending on their sex or the gender, I should say, would have no reason to believe that anything sinister or nefarious is being planned. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the impression that -- that is Y's -- that is the underlying impression of the conversation from correspondent Y.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And we have no reason to know what he or she actually knows, but all we have is this particular intercept, and that's all we have, correct, between these two at this given time?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I mean I believe that you can derive from the context exactly what Y is aware of, and that that's fair.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if I can show you 192, P192. Again, I have it if you don't.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have it, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. This conversation takes place 5 -- 10 minutes after the earlier intercept. And again, assuming that these intercepts are true, accurate, and complete. And here, there seems to be, to coin your term, a voice compromise. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, certainly in this respect, the compromise is with respect to rank, at least in the text, it says "General." I don't believe that it says in the text "General Mladic." So in this particular case, the identification of Mladic is based off of the operator.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, is there anything in this text that would give the impression that this is indeed General Mladic?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I believe from the tone and the directives that this is, in fact, General Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And this is based on your observation of him on videos, the manner in which he's behaved; and from that, and the circumstances at the time, and that's how you've arrived at this conclusion? And some information from the operators that on occasion they would be able to identify particular key individuals because of their distinctive speech pattern?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I rely on that far more than some of my own perceived psychological skills in evaluating General Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm very comfortable with the identification from the operators in this respect.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And -- okay. Do we know who X is?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not believe that in this X is identified.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. So in other words, you do not know?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Do you know where X might be?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And from here, General Mladic seems to be indicating something slightly different from the fellow or from the conversation that we went through earlier in P191. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So assuming this is General Mladic, he seems to have made up his mind, if we are to believe this intercept at face value, that those individuals that are gathered at Potocari will have no choice and, in fact, all of them will have to be transported out. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And you don't have anything that would tell us that this state of mind, assuming it was General Mladic, and assuming that that was indeed his state of mind at the time, you don't have anything that would allow us to know that this state of mind was passed on to Mr. Trisic who was acting at the time as the assistant commander of rear services who was also assisting in carrying out orders that he had received from the higher organ, the assistant of the rear services of the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. I have no information that would be able to expand on the state of mind issue of Major Trisic in that respect.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, just getting back to Major Trisic for just slightly, and we're just using this as an example, but I want to go back to the functional relationships because we had that little quarrel; hopefully we're past it. But what I was focussing on is when a higher echelon organ is going to a lower echelon organ acting on an order which has been ordered from the top, you would not expect under these rules that the lower echelon organ would need to get authorisation - that's the operative word - authorisation from his immediate commander?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, Mr. Karnavas, with respect to how broad or how narrow that order was, it will depend.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm glad that you said that because we may not disagree here. If the request is narrow, in other words, it's within the original request, and if it's sufficiently narrow that it can be carried out without compromise, if I can use that term, without compromise to the organ itself, the lower echelon organ, that then one would not expect the assistant commander of rear services to have to go to his commander and say: "What do you think about this? Have you authorised it" and what have you. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that is one possibility. Just the same with, you know, another possibility would very well be going back to P434 where because of this broad envelope of the order that has come from the Drina Corps to the Bratunac Brigade, the assumption that the commander will be aware of the general intent behind it, that the rear services' officer could then carry out specific components of that and would not have to check back. I mean, that is --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- That's all in that same general envelope.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. If on the other hand, and I think this is where perhaps we got off a little bit astray, and it might have been because we were a little bit excited, or at least on my part, if, however, the order to the lower echelon organ is such that in essence it would compromise the resources, compromise that particular organ, in other words, the request is of such nature, even though it's within the general confines of the order from the higher-up, but what is being requested would really affect the functioning and capabilities of the lower organ, then in all likelihood we can conclude or we would expect, I should say, that the assistant commander would go to his own commander and say "I just received this order. It really will drain us of our resources. It will gut us out." I think that was the word that you used. "What should I do?"
