At which point then in time the commander himself would step in to speak to his commander to see if the situation could be resolved.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In part, and in the other part it is also if that request is going to breach outside of the competency, so it's not just a question of overtaxing the specific organ, but it's also an issue of if it were going to -- in order to accomplish that task, that there would be coordination or there will have to be assistance from other staff organs. So he would have to broaden that. But I mean, back to your specific instance, yeah, that would be one instance where he would go back to the commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And in this -- in the context in which we are speaking of in those days, what was being requested of Mr. Trisic was not outside the competency of that particular organ, was it?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Strictly speaking, no, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And strictly speaking, what was being asked of him, keeping in mind all the other things that are about to happen as far as where the fuel will come from, where the buses will come from, what was being asked of him, the assistance that the rear services of the Drina Corps was requesting directly of the rear services of the Bratunac Brigade, was not going to overtax the Bratunac Brigade rear services, was it?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would disagree with that statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And how so? Let's deal with that disagreement so we can clear up the air before we go on to the next topic.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Assuming in this instance that the Bratunac Brigade was tasked and that the rear services branch was administering the buses and fuel issue, certainly as noted in P434 --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: P434, which one is that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the 12 July one on fuel, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Because you're throwing these things at me, and --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm going to go slow for everybody.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: As long as I know what exactly you're talking about. Okay.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The issue of fuel especially 10.000 litres of diesel and 2.000 litres of petrol, were going to far outstrip the holdings of the Bratunac Infantry Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Let me stop you right there for a second. With respect to the fuel, because I put it in the greater context the way normally you like to, we knew with respect to fuel that on the 11th, there was some discussion -- or the 12th some discussion with the UN with regard to the fuel. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And we know that the arrangement, which the parties had agreed to, was that the VRS would provide the fuel, and at some point, they will be reimbursed of that fuel by the UN. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And we know -- we know that fuel came from outside the Bratunac area, do we not, in order to pump fuel into those 50-some buses and trucks that came?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. My understanding is that it came from the Vihor fuel facility which is in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Let's assume it came strictly from them. Is that an asset or a resource of the Bratunac Brigade? Yes or no. And we'll discuss it, but just --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not strictly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: What do you mean "not strictly"? Is that a military asset?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. So in other words, the commander of the Bratunac Brigade just can't rely on that as his private reserve, can he?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whether he can rely on it as his private reserve, it is reflected in their own evaluation that they recognised that 75 per cent of their fuel needs, particularly from the period 1 January to 1 July of 1995, came from Vihor, and that only 25 per cent come from the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But we're not talking about that. What I'm talking about --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection. He interrupted the witness while the witness was still trying to explain.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I thought he was finished. I thought he was finished.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And also, the interpreters, we wouldn't have a problem if we could have a slight delay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: That's the problem with these proceedings, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Guilty as charged, Your Honour. I will --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Take your time. Take your time. It's different from any domestic jurisdictions. I know that we'll lose the gist of cross-examination, I know that. But you have to take your time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You're right. You're absolutely correct, Your Honour, absolutely correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If you want to complete your thought. If not, I can go on to the next one.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I'm not trying to fight, but what I'm trying to explain is that, you know, getting back to what was the original question as to whether or not these issues fall strictly in the scope of the competence of rear service to a point where he wouldn't feel a need to brief his commander, and then you asked me to explain the implied task behind a lot of this. And that's what I'm trying to do, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, let's put it into the context. You have Mladic on the ground. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You have General Zivanovic or Krstic, General Krstic, who would have been the next in line on the ground. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of July, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And now you have Acamovic coming directly to Trisic making a request that he has received from his higher-ups.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We also know that there has been an announcement for trucks and buses to come to Bratunac. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are orders to that effect. Not announcements, but certainly with respect to the military, they're orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. You're correct in one part and incorrect in another. There were orders to the military, but were there not also announcements for the civilian resources of buses and trucks to come?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were the orders for the military. There were the orders from the RSMOD.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The RSMOD --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Ministry of Defence, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the requisitions of civilian assets. I understand, although I've not ever seen the text of such, that there may have been public announcements over the airwaves for people to send stuff.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You are aware, and we talked about this Territorial Defence concept and All People's Defence concept. Right?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did have a discussion on that, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And you're aware that in fact the folks that lived in Bosnia-Herzegovina, in fact, the folks that lived in the former Yugoslavia would often go through drills in order to comply with requests for assistance when there would be natural catastrophes or natural disasters or the need of such assistance. Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I take your word for it. Again, I'm not very versed in the pre-war TO relationship and how that works. So I mean, I'll take your word for it on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Perhaps that's why -- perhaps that's why, and we'll get to that throughout the process of the trial, the mobilisation process of getting the Department of Defence to make the request for trucks and buses to come to assist was able to be achieved with some efficiency. Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't connect the two. The Republika Srpska Ministry of Defence, by their own law, the law on defence, is charged with the ability to do that. I don't see how it's connected to a former TO structure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, the law is an extension or a -- in any event, I don't want to get into that discussion. But if we stick with the law itself, the law -- and the Ministry of Defence is a civilian branch, is it not?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Minister of Defence rotated -- not rotated, but at various points he was military and civilian. But I believe they tried to organise the Ministry of Defence as a civilian branch as much as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And the request was to the civilian authorities to assist in providing buses and trucks. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know it's couched a request. It says an order. If it says a request, I'm incorrect. But it's an order.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: An order, then. It's even stronger. They ordered them. The government had the power to order civilian authorities to provide buses and trucks forthwith. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. They came out of the state-owned businesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Which may explain -- which may explain as to why those buses and trucks arrived there in such a short period of time. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Which may also explain as to how fuel was able to get there, or if it was there, to be used that belonged to the civilian authorities and be used by the military in order to carry out this particular task which we all agree was a looming, humanitarian crisis at the time. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, that may be a possibility. I do not have any data as to the mechanics of exactly how or under what circumstances the fuel was made available. But clearly, we do have the records that it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And finally, you don't have any records to suggest, do you, that the fuel that was needed for that period of time, the buses and the trucks, was within the capabilities of the Bratunac Brigade? In other words, they had sufficient storage of fuel to meet those demands?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't believe that they did have the -- brigade's own fuel. It was nowhere near sufficient.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that's a fair statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And it would also be fair that when the issue of fuel comes up and, for instance, Major Trisic is involved in his discussions with I believe it's Lieutenant Colonel Acamovic, that those two, given that they're from the same organ, higher echelon to lower echelon, would probably put their two heads together and perhaps meet with the local authorities in order to ensure that the fuel is there for the trucks and buses. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. I expect that they would have coordinated to ensure that the buses and trucks that were coming in were going to be fueled, or the ones that needed to be fueled. And in fact, you know, the records that we have indicates that there was a successful process to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. And I guess the point that I'm trying to drive straight through the other end is that there was no need for Major Trisic to get authorisation from his commander to assist his -- to assist Lieutenant Colonel Acamovic of the higher echelon organ to which he belonged to in this particular case, was there? There was no need.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Given that on that particular day they were talking about a dispersal of, I think, approximately 6.000 litres of fuel and that that's well over the normal consumption of the brigade, I don't know that I could make that logical conclusion. I think that it would be enough of an event that there would have to be some wider discussion of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And when we throw into the mix that you have I believe General Krstic was on the ground, would we not -- can we not conclude that Trisic would have expected, assumed, presumed, or at least expected that if an order came directly to him from Lieutenant Colonel Acamovic, that that order had been precleared and that he was to act upon it as expeditiously as humanly possible?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Major Trisic is allowed to assume that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And so as we stand here today, as we stand here today, and when I repeat myself, it's not for the sake of hearing myself twice, it's for the sake of driving the point home, but when we sit here today, we cannot say with any degree of certainty that Major Trisic had to get authorisation or received authorisation or even went to get clearance or even went to inform Colonel Blagojevic before he carried out a lawful order as he was required to do on that particular day that was issued to him by the higher echelon organ?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection. That assumes fact not in evidence, that this is a lawful order. I don't know why that needs to be thrown into the question. I don't mind the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, witness, answer the question, bearing in mind there's no "lawful" word before that order.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir, it is a fair assumption. We have no data on that one way or another. It is a fair assumption.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And, sir, I guess just to put the finishing touches on this, the character of the relationship between the organs of a higher echelon and those of the lower echelon are one of a staff relationship. Isn't that a fact? And I'm --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. I mean, that sounds like that's language right out of the regulation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It is, it is. I'm pounding it home. And this relationship, the staff relationship, is actually more of a functional relationship governed by the principles of obligatory action - that's the language that I'm reading from - obligatory actions in accordance with the request of the staff organ of the superior command for the purpose of implementing the decision made by the superior commander. Isn't that what we're talking about and have been talking about for the last hour or so?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. I mean, you're talking about the proper application of the command and staff process. I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And on its face, on its face at least, one might gather that there is an alternative chain of command that is permitted within these particular rules that govern the JNA and the VRS who observed those rules and implemented more or less many of those rules. And this is one of them. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, if you do not have a military background, I can see where you can come to that conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Well, we'll argue that point some other time. But let me ask you this: As a comparative purpose, for comparative purposes, because we know that there was some emphasis placed with respect -- with respect to the intercept that we have between General Krstic and Beara from the Main Staff where he is requesting assistance because he has yet to deliver approximately 3500 parcels, that one. Do you recall? I don't have the number handy.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am familiar with the discussion, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And if you do have the number, maybe, you know, just for the record so we have a record of that. But in any event, we'll get to it. As I recall your testimony, you used that as an example of showing how the system worked. In other words, you implied or concluded that since Beara needed some assistance, he did not merely reach out -- he did not merely reach out to the Zvornik Brigade or the Bratunac Brigade or the Milici Brigade and just take their assets; but instead, he called -- he called General Krstic. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And you said here is how the system works because General Krstic then said: "I can't pull some folks out of this area because it will disturb the access, but why don't you check with Nastic or Blagojevic." Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where I made the point that it is how the system works is in illustrating that even in this instance, as Colonel Beara, who was involved - and I think that's not a point of contention - in unlawful acts, was not able to operate outside of his own competence and had to get the authority from the higher commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Exactly. And one of the reasons is because there was no functional relationship there.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not catching your point, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Maybe you could help me out. Colonel Beara is with the security services. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, he has -- he has a functional relationship with the security services of the lower echelon, and that would have been the Drina Corps. So he would have gone to Popovic if he needed them to act upon an order which he had received, that is, Mladic -- or Beara had received from Mladic. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. In that respect, he would have -- his functional subordinate would have been Popovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And below Popovic, he could reach even further down and grab Nikolic if he so needed to go that further down the chain because of this functional relationship which we talked about today. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. I mean, in theory it would be Popovic going to Nikolic, but there could be a skip. I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And because of his position and because of where he was coming from, he could easily even reach further down below Nikolic right to the military police which are, in essence, part of or controlled by or directed by the security organ within a brigade. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would disagree there because while they are, in fact, controlled by and directed by the security organ, they again fall as an asset of the commander. So again, while it's situation-dependant, that is not a blanket statement I'm prepared to agree to.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And I might have gotten carried away there. I might have been overbroad. But you would agree with me, would you not, that generally speaking Nikolic would be tasking the military police?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: He is responsible for their day-to-day functions and that would include tasking, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And Popovic is looked upon or could be looked upon by others as the superior commander, at least within the organ, within that functional relationship, Popovic would be looked upon as the superior of Nikolic. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Within that staff chain, he would be considered the superior of Nikolic, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And within that staff chain, Mladic would be looked upon as both the superior of Popovic and Nikolic. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that context, I mean, Mladic is the commander both through the command chain and indirectly through his staff chain. However, again, Beara, and then on top of Beara, Tolimir, so there are a couple more levels.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay, all right, we're not going all the way up the food chain. I'm going to stop at Beara. So when Beara goes to a military police officer or when Popovic goes to the head of the military police and makes a demand, is it not reasonable, is it not reasonable to conclude that they must act upon that demand? Or to put it more precisely, that order?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that would probably be their first instinct. They would receive the order from a colonel and would follow it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, getting back to our example, in this particular intercept, Beara, Beara - and I believe for the record it's P245 - Beara is not asking Krstic, General Krstic, to use the security organ or to use the military police. He's asking for any help that he can get which we could imply are soldiers themselves. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's a fair implication.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And those soldiers that he's requesting are outside, outside the structural, the functional relationship. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Presumably the subordinate units are outside of his functional relationship, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And that's why he cannot just reach out and grab some of them without going through the proper chain of command. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And in fact, if he had done so or if one would do that in that situation, because of the lack of functional relationship, the lower echelon individual, be he a soldier or an officer, might not necessarily respond in the same fashion, almost instinctively, reflexively as, say, for instance when Popovic would go to the military police and ask them to do something?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suspect that for a young officer or a soldier who's given an order by a colonel, that there would be an urge to respond to it obviously. However, in the particular case, because -- assuming that they knew who Colonel Beara was and, of course, assuming that they knew he was outside the functional area, what would have happened or should have happened would be that that commander or soldier basically goes back to his immediate superior and says: "I have received this order from this colonel. Do I carry it out, sir?"

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: So that is the more practical application of, I believe, the point you're getting to.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. One is reflex because there is a functional relationship. The other is pause, pause. Perhaps -- perhaps some consultation with their immediate superior, though perhaps because of Colonel Beara's personality and charisma, if he had any, if he had any, they may have reacted. Okay --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, sir, the assumption is that the people, depending on how far down the chain of command he's going to ask, you can't make the assumption that they will know him on sight.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: So they're going to respond as in they're getting an order from a colonel. It is not the guidance that they last received from their own superior. And they're going to, as a matter of practice, want to contact their own superior officer to find out if what they're receiving it an order that they ought to follow.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the speaker kindly slow down, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My apologies.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: For once you're guilty and not me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, we said that scenario you gave us is because they're outside the functional relationship, and one would not expect that pause, that refrain, say, from the military police who would instinctively act upon an order from Popovic or even Nikolic, and certainly from Beara because that's who normally tasks them. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say certainly from Nikolic and Popovic. And again, Beara, it may well be: Do they know who he is? He is not a visible figure in Bratunac. But with respect to Nikolic and Popovic, I conclude that these are people that the military police officers should know on sight.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now I think we can move on. Just to bring us back a little bit to Potocari, we have these refugees, some of whom will become prisoners, if I could use that term, in Potocari. On that day --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: 12 July, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: 12 July. 12 July. Whose are they? Are they the Main Staff? Are they the Drina Corps's? Or are the Bratunac Brigade's? They're not an asset. They certainly are a liability. They need to deal with them. Who is in control, in charge? Who is responsible for all of these folks that have gathered in Potocari as a result of Krivaja 1995?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: If that question could be broken down. There are several conflicting things, who do they belong to, whose responsibility? These are all different things, and it's an important area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I agree. I'm just trying to speed the process up, Your Honour. But I'll break it down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I think the question asked by the counsel is a proper one. And the -- we all get the point in this question. We will see how the witness is going to answer this question. If there's need to reput the question, you may do that, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In theory, they belong to the VRS. As a course of my analysis in the investigation, and I don't like to use the phrase "ownership" obviously, whom they are in custody of at any given time remains an open question. Logically, the Bratunac Brigade, as the unit on the ground and the unit with the bulk of the resources would play a large part in that. The Drina Corps, at that time chief of staff, and their other staff officers will also play a part in that, as will the Main Staff officers who play a part of it. So I don't think that you can say that they are in the custody of this echelon at this point in time and under these particular circumstances. It's just not there. I mean, certainly we've not had witnesses come forward from the various military organisations and claim where the prisoners or whose specific custody they are in. So given the information that I have, there is no specific answer to your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. I guess we're going to have to reclaim some ground that I thought we had gained yesterday, and now we seem to have lost. And I'm talking about zone of responsibility. See, I'm trying to move forward. Okay. Now, I believe, and correct me if I'm wrong, that we talked about as far as two days ago that it was your answer that if you have the zone of responsibility on the map with respect to the Bratunac Brigade, a concept which I vehemently disagree with, but nonetheless, if we accept that, if we accept that, you had indicated that other units could be working inside that zone. In fact, we see -- we saw an example of another brigade actually having or presumably having its zone of responsibility inside that area. And you had indicated that when they are working, operating inside the zone of responsibility of another brigade, of the Bratunac Brigade in this instance, that the Bratunac Brigade would not have any control or command over those units. Now, that's the long and short of it. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. If they weren't given subordination of those units, they don't have command of them. I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. So now, that is going to be our point of departure as we try to regain the ground that we seem to have lost.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I just go back to my previous objection. Mr. Karnavas's question had three parts to it that I can recall. One had to do with ownership, and that's, as Mr. Butler said, that's difficult to figure out what that means in a military context. It had to do with control, which we've heard a lot about, and it had to do with responsibility. Mr. Butler, it's hard to tell which three of those he was responding to, but I think it was mostly the one having to do with ownership. Now, there has been assumption by Mr. Karnavas that he was talking about responsibility, and now he's being cross-examined on the issue of responsibility. There's -- that's the problem. We can't tell what Mr. Butler said about responsibility because there was three parts in that question, and I don't know if -- he might even agree with Mr. Karnavas. So that was my problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'd like to respond.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I understand that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I would like to respond, Your Honour. Because Mr. Butler here finally, you know, we're connecting. He's understanding my questions. And certainly Mr. Butler is not shy of voicing his opinion if he doesn't understand me or if he thinks my question is too complex or I'm asking too much of him. And so I'm trying to be kinder and gentler. This is why I've taken this tack. I'll break it down. I'll break it down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I think Mr. Butler answered your question just for the first part, the question of the ownership.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Maybe we'll come to the next two issues. One is about control and the other is about responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We are, Your Honour. We are. We're going step by step here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, now that we have that in mind, in this area that you have mapped out as zone of responsibility for the Bratunac Brigade --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, I didn't map it out. It's on the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I agree. It's on the map that you have accepted --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can Mr. Butler be allowed to answer the three-part question? He was asked a question containing three parts on the fifth day of cross-examination. To expect Mr. Butler to take apart three key parts of this entire case is too much. And if he wants to set that question aside and make that clear, fine. But I don't want it to come back and be argued later on that Mr. Butler's answer had to do with responsibility because that's the possible interpretation when left like this. Multipart questions are a cancer to this system.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm not going to respond to the Prosecution today. I'm going to -- I'm going to refrain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I want that on the record that I'm refraining.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Butler, we've just covered this morning, and a little bit yesterday, that in this area that the map that shows the zone of responsibility for the Bratunac Brigade, a concept which you seem to agree with, though it's not in the rules, you have indicated that in that area you had the Main Staff operating, you had the Drina Corps operating, and you had the Bratunac Brigade operating during this relevant period that we're discussing. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: You had the Bratunac Brigade operating. You had the Drina Corps command and staff, elements of them there. And you had the Main Staff commander there. So in that sense, they're all operating in that zone, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. So the answer is yes. Now, you indicated yesterday, and I think we covered it a little bit today, that General Mladic was in command and control. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. In fact, you basically said yesterday that wherever he goes, he's usually in command and control. I understand that was in a loose sense that you said it. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: General Mladic as the commander of the army is in command of the army whether he's physically on the ground at a location or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But in this instance and I think we covered this a little bit, General Mladic is micro-managing, somewhat, is he not?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: He is giving direct orders in a lot of cases; I guess that qualifies as micro-management.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. But not only is he micro-managing, but he is directly involved, directly involved, in negotiating with the UN, the DutchBat, as well as the folks that were representing the Muslim population that had gathered in Potocari. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And he made all the decisions. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. He indicated what was on -- what was going to happen next. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And in fact, he issued orders to that effect.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And we talked about it a little bit because remember I mentioned Pandurevic had that little concern about the 28th, and you are quite right to say no, they were able to calm him down, to say let's not go all the way to Potocari, let's hold off. He listened to them. But then we know that after the second meeting, after the second meeting or during the second meeting, a decision was made with respect to arranging for the transportation of those who wished to leave out of Potocari and on to the free territory. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. He made the decision I presume between the second meeting and the third meeting because that's when you see the manifestation of orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes. And now we see a manifestation of orders that directly reflect his intent.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And those orders were passed down the chain of command. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And one of the orders, I don't know if we have a direct one, but at least one of the orders, it would appear directed certain folks to go to Potocari on that particular day. "Folks," what I'm talking about are VRS. You don't need to read.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I guess what you're asking is -- we're assuming that it was Mladic's direction was that members of the VRS were to go to Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Couldn't put it any better than that.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And I take it he had some orders -- he had given some orders with respect to what would happen once they got to Potocari. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that. I'm not aware of -- there were some orders with respect to the orders we do know that he gave Colonel Borovcanin with respect to his forces entering Potocari. I'm not aware -- I'm trying to think back, but I'm not aware of many instances that are coming to mind of direct orders from Mladic to other army members with that respect.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, according to Nikolic, if one is to believe him, members of the 65th Protection Regiment, I believe, were there, and that would have been at least a Main Staff asset. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I do understand that. But I have with a video and everything else, I have no evidence that puts them there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. So he must either be mistaken or misrepresenting the truth on that one?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those are two options. And the third one is that he is correct, and I have no evidence to corroborate it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. So those are the universe of choices. And throughout the years of your investigation, did you come across anything that would give you the impression that they were, in fact, there because Momir Nikolic tells us that he even was coordinating their actions as well as the actions of others that were there? And I'm sure you read his testimony before you came here.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did read his testimony. And through the course of the investigation, there is no evidence that puts the 65th Protection Regiment in Potocari certainly on 12 July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Nor is there any evidence that he was coordinating the 65th Regiment over there on that particular day, is there?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I guess that is the next logical conclusion to the fact that I can't put them there. Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, there were units from the Drina Corps, were there not, over there?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: For 12 July?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't believe so, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. So if Momir Nikolic was saying he was also coordinating those units that might be there, that would also be a misrepresentation, maybe an honest mistake on his part, or maybe you just haven't come across anything to verify Nikolic, "the coordinator" on that particular day in Potocari, that and the next day?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 13th, some of the Drina Corps units, or at least one of them -- elements goes through the city or through Potocari. But on the 12th, I don't believe that there were Drina Corps units per se in Potocari. The staff officers of the Drina Corps were there --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Drina Wolves?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was one instance from a Dutch Battalion officer who I believe -- he saw individuals who he believes might have been Drina Wolves who might have been there on the 12th, but that's the only thing I've heard of it. And that conflicts with the other evidence I have that puts the Drina Wolves in the Bandera triangle with the remainder of the other units on 12 July. So that's why there's not much coming to mind with respect to Drina Corps units in Potocari on 12 July.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: What about the 10th Sabotage Detachment, I think that's the correct -- or 10th Sabotage Division, I'm sorry?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's a Main Staff asset.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Were they there?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't believe so. I think that at least according to the testimony of Erdemovic that the majority of them stayed in Srebrenica because they were given a follow-on mission afterwards to clear the Sase mine complex or the tunnel that runs from it to the town because they believed that there might be things in there. I understand that maybe one or two Dutch witnesses believe that they saw them there, but I believe that they were in Srebrenica that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, we're almost ready for our break, so we're going to have to continue this issue about the prisoners and what have you. But just one last question: It sounds to me, and I think the Trial Chamber would be very interested in this, it sounds to me that from reading at least that portion of Nikolic's testimony, you are befuddled because you don't know, you don't have any evidence that would support that portion of his testimony which he gave under oath before our Honourable Members of this Trial Chamber. Would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I'm looking on the screen here. I'm not befuddled, but I agree that there isn't evidence that would corroborate that portion of his testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And there is no evidence to corroborate that, one might conclude that it was a mere fabrication under oath normally known in the legal parlance as perjury. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is one conclusion that might be drawn, sir. I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think at this point, because I'm about to launch into another segment, and this might be a good time to break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we'll resume at 12.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, before you start your cross-examination, I think there's a scheduling ruling that this Trial Chamber would like to make. This morning, Ms. Sinatra asked for two days for the cross-examination of this witness, which was unexpected by this Bench. But we'll do our best to accommodate their request, if possible. So they ask for two days. That will be six sittings, altogether 450 minutes for their cross-examination. The time at their disposal for their cross-examination is only 330 minutes at most, which means that it's more or less about four sittings altogether. Is that all right, Ms. Sinatra?

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Your Honour, Mr. Stojanovic will be doing the cross. But in all honesty, you know, the team from Mr. Blagojevic got five days to cross, minimum, and maybe more. It's totally up to Mr. Stojanovic, but I think that from looking at the material and working on the cross together, I think he's going to need two full days. I'll let Mr. Stojanovic address the Court on that matter since he's going to be doing the cross, but there's a lot of material to cover in Mr. Butler's report, and especially the annex including the Zvornik Brigade is most important.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honours. I have been waiting for six days to start my own cross-examination. When we started out, I once told the Prosecutor that I expected to have an opportunity to use up to one and a half days to cross-examine this witness. This keeps changing on a minute-to-minute basis. Depending on Mr. Karnavas's cross-examination, some of his questions causing an overlap in relation to resubordination, control, and command. I will be able to leave these questions out as a consequence. But then again, I have several new areas that have cropped up that need clarifying. I would like to use the transcript of Mr. Karnavas's cross-examination of Mr. Butler to ask a number of questions of my own. At any rate, I will fully observe the Court's decision. I hope I can fit my cross-examination into one and a half days, or 330 minutes, as you said, four blocks, four sessions. Roughly speaking, I think that's the time I need to cross-examine this witness. As for our exhibits, we have about 20 exhibits we are preparing to tender into evidence. We think we can deal with this in a quick and efficient manner. Mr. Butler's answers are very succinct. I don't think we'll need to waste a lot of time going over the same questions. So my estimate is that I can indeed manage to complete my cross-examination within the 330 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much indeed for your cooperation. Mr. McCloskey, how much time do you think you need for the redirect?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Very little as yet. 30 minutes, maybe an hour at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: But you have to leave some time for the Judges to ask some questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: 30 minutes is -- doesn't seem too long, Your Honour. And I hope I don't go there because I think at this point your questions are critical, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Here's the scheduling order at this stage for next week: Next week Monday, we'll sit in the Courtroom II starting from 9.00 until 1.45 in the morning. I hope during this time, Mr. Karnavas will finish his cross-examination. And in the afternoon, we will continue to sit from 3.00 to 6.30. And then Mr. Stojanovic will start their cross-examination. On Tuesday, it's a UN holiday; we do not sit. On Wednesday, we'll start at 2.15 in the afternoon, continue the cross-examination by Mr. Stojanovic. And in that afternoon, there are two sittings allocated for the cross-examination for Mr. Stojanovic. So all together, there will be 330 minutes for Mr. Jokic's Defence. And for the last 75 minutes, we'll conduct the redirect, Judges' questions, admission of the evidence. We'll send this witness home Wednesday night. On Thursday, we'll start in the morning session, from 9.00 to 1.45 in Courtroom II. On Friday, also in the morning, 9.00 to 1.45 in Courtroom I. It is so decided. Mr. Karnavas, you may continue your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Butler, we were discussing the issue of prisoners, and we're trying to figure that conundrum as to whose prisoners they were. Now, let me go back a little bit and cover some of the points that we covered yesterday or the day before. As I understand it, we discussed that the order that was issued by the Drina Corps of the 2nd, the preparatory order, I believe, of July 2nd required or ordered that the prisoners be dealt by the security sector. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The security section was given the authority to deal with the issue of selecting the locations for prisoners and -- I mean, I'd like to get to the exact phrase on that. That's why I'm not --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you want to get that out?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we have it, it would probably be the best thing. I don't want to misstate that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: To be honest, I wasn't planning on going to the actual document, but we might be able to put our hands on it. Let me go to the next document which would have been the order that was drafted by the commander of the Bratunac Brigade. If you recall, we discussed that where it was indicated that the prisoners that were, if any were to be captured by the Bratunac Brigade, they would be taken to Pribicevac, and that's where they would be stored or held until -- at least that's all we know. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. It was directed that any prisoners taken would be brought to Pribicevac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And we indicated yesterday, did we not, that we have no knowledge or no proof, nothing that would verify that any prisoners were indeed captured by the Bratunac Brigade from the 6th to the 11th. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, sir. There's no data on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Although to be fair with you and the record, you indicated that there may have been; we just don't know. But certainly there's nothing that would reflect either in the daily reports to the -- either the daily reports to the Drina Corps or the Drina Corps daily reports to the Main Staff that prisoners were captured by the Bratunac Brigade. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, sir, it's not reflected in the Bratunac reports, and we do not have the Drina Corps reports. So I can't answer the second part of that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And throughout your investigation over all of these years, yours and OTP's and everybody else involved, there has never been any information, any documentation, nothing, in fact, that would reflect that prisoners were captured by the Bratunac Brigade from the 6th to the 11th. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And that may be one strong indicator, would it not, that would at least allow us to draw a conclusion that in all likelihood there is no documentation anywhere because no prisoners were ever taken by the Bratunac Brigade during that period of time. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is an indicator, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, we have a situation that changes from the 11th with respect to the overall situation in Srebrenica and in Potocari. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And from the -- sometime on the 11th, perhaps as early as the 10th, I don't want to get into all the specifics, but at some point the population of Srebrenica begins to move, those who haven't gone in -- with the exception of the column, begin to move for security and safety to where the UN DutchBat are located and they eventually find themselves in Potocari. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. Most of the movement begins on the morning of the 11th and continues through the day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And of course, we indicated that those who chose not to go there, many of whom were members of the 28th Division, others who were not, gathered elsewhere, and then began to go towards the free territory at some point. And we usually or we have been referring to them as "the column" for lack of a more precise term. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And we talked about briefly that on the night of the 11th and the night of the 12th that there was some uncertainty as to where the 28th Division was located, and this column. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: At some point, there were some indicators as to where -- that a column had been seen. And in fact, we discussed a little bit, and I think we were able to come to a mutual conclusion that they were able to leave the 1st, the 2nd, and the 3rd Battalion areas without incident. And by that, I mean without coming into contact with the Bratunac Brigade. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: On 12 July -- or on 11 and 12 July, they did not come into contact with these three battalions, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And in fact, it is not until they get towards the 4th Battalion that they seem to have been identified, the column, that is, and at some point, I believe it's around the 13th or so, that we actually have some contact, not necessarily with the 4th Battalion, but with the Zvornik Brigade and the column. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection. That's a misstatement of the evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm asking the gentleman to give his answer, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Not misstate the evidence. That is fundamental to the process. There is evidence in this Court to the contrary of that. Perhaps he's forgotten it. But that is a misstatement of the evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'll rephrase.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You may rephrase it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'll rephrase.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: On the 11th, did the 4th Battalion attack the column? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: On the 12th, did the 4th Battalion attack the column? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: On the 13th, was there an attack by the 4th Battalion of the Bratunac Brigade against the column? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was contact, but not an attack.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And what do you mean by "contact"?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is my understanding that the 4th Battalion came into contact with some members of the column and that at least one Bosnian Muslim was taken prisoner by them on the 13th.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That's correct. But other than that, there was no battle to speak of between the 4th and the column on the 13th? And by that, what I mean is as we know later on what's going to happen later on on the 14th and the 15th between the column and the Zvornik Brigade. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely nothing of that intensity.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. So at least on the 11th and the 12th, because now I want you -- or the 12th and the 13th, I want to bring you back to Potocari. It would appear, would it not, that the Bratunac Brigade has not taken a single prisoner that we are aware of? Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: With respect to the members of the column, on the 11th and 12th, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, what about with respect to what happened on the battlefield?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what I am referring to with "the column".

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, are you aware of any prisoners that were actually physically taken by the Bratunac Brigade and then taken to Pribicevac on the 13th where the commander had designated all prisoners should be taken in the event they were -- any were captured?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Why would they take them to Pribicevac on the 13th?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, I'm asking you --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, no, they certainly wouldn't do that. By that point in time, all operations had shifted away from Pribicevac and were at Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So the answer is they didn't take any Pribicevac? I'm just doing it by a process of elimination, sir.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, no, sir, I have no knowledge of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. And do you have any knowledge of the Bratunac Brigade on its own, and I'm not talking about the Drina Corps or the Main Staff or any of them or any prisoners bought by them and taken elsewhere. Were you aware of any prisoners captured by members of the Bratunac Brigade on the 13th?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, the issue that I'm aware of on the 13th is the continued separation of Muslim men in Potocari and their movement into Bratunac, into facilities.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, let's stick with that. We talked about earlier that Mladic was in command and in control. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Who ordered the separation of the men? Was it Colonel Blagojevic? Was it General Krstic or General Zivanovic? Or was it General Mladic? Or none of the above?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that as a result of the third meeting on the morning of the 12th, it was General Mladic who had indicated that men were going to be screened for war crimes. So I guess that answers your question. It would be General Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And would it not be fair to conclude, then, since General Mladic is there on the ground and in fact later on we see him in Potocari where he's doing a photo op of such, and also making some statements for public consumption, some of which -- some of which would have been heard by those around him, including any military police from the Bratunac Brigade that happened to be there as his guard and as the regulations warranted, okay. Is it not a fact that at that point in time, that it's General Mladic that is still in command and control of the situation?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: General Mladic, again, he's always in command and control. And the situation is occurring pursuant to his orders, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And so the question is who, who is responsible for all of those people that have gathered in Potocari on that day?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the highest level, it would be General Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Who is there on the ground. Right?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And is running the show?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: He is indisputably directing traffic, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And right beneath him you have the Drina Corps. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And at some point it is the Drina Corps that is assisting at least -- or I should say directing the movement -- I should say facilitating, that's a better term, facilitating the exodus by coordinating the buses incoming to Potocari, the fueling of the buses, and of course having the women and children getting on the buses and ultimately taken out of Potocari to a safer area. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In part, the Drina Corps rear services people were there and were facilitating the buses and ensuring that they were fueled and getting them to Potocari. For the second part of your question, getting on the buses, I don't believe that those same Drina Corps officers were involved in that process.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And I understand you indicated also that MUP was there. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. There was at least one company of the Jahorina MUP training centre that had been there, and the Court has heard evidence on that. And there was at least for a portion of the time the members of the 2nd Sekovici detachment of the MUP special brigade that were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Who made the decision, incidentally, for the men that were separated to be taken, and to be secured in Bratunac? Who made that decision? If you know.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the answer to that based on the documents or intercept. And I know that some witnesses have talked about that, and I will leave it at that. But I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But you do know, you do know that it wasn't Colonel Blagojevic, don't you?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that. I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Sir, given those who were there, given those officers that were running the show, when we look at the chain of command process, or to put it in a pedestrian fashion, the pecking order, clearly, clearly Colonel Blagojevic, the commander of the Bratunac Brigade, was well below on that order, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was the third echelon commander, Mladic, the Drina Corps's Zivanovic, and then him. He was the third echelon commander in this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: By your indication, his headquarters, in his headquarters, he was hosting or they had taken -- he was hosting, let's leave it at that, the Drina Corps and the Main Staff as well. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And the Main Staff as well as the Drina Corps could use the facilities whenever they wanted. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: They could use his communications whenever they wanted?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: They could order his staff to a certain extent whenever they wanted, could they not?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It depends on exactly what that certain extent is, and we've discussed that. So I don't want to make it that broad. But they -- you know, within their functional confines, they could direct his staff to do things.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And when they wanted to, for instance, have something sent and they wanted it coded so it could be sent off, they could do that through the communications centre. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I believe that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And so would it not be fair, sir, to conclude that for all intents and purposes, Colonel Blagojevic as the commander of the Bratunac Brigade during those days, while he may have been the commander on paper, was hardly commanding anybody in Potocari on the 11th or the 12th or the 13th? Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I disagree.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And he was hardly in control, was he?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have evidence that suggests that he was not in command or control of his subordinate units, and I've never suggested that he was in command or control of units that weren't subordinate to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And where were his subordinate units, sir? They were still out there on that defensive, static line, were they not?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Let him answer the question, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It's a misstatement of the evidence. That's fundamental. You cannot misstate the evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I believe that this question is very important to the Defence. Let us hear what the witness is going to tell us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: He can qualify the answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe that there is video evidence that shows a number of individuals from the 2nd Infantry battalion in Potocari on the 12th. I believe some of that video evidence also shows members of the Bratunac Brigade military police there on the 12th. So in that respect, they were not all on the defence line. There were a number that were in Potocari on the 12th.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, let's talk about the military police. We indicated that some of them were there as a result of Mladic. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: You had offered that possibility, and I said given that they are guarding him, that that's a fair conclusion, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: What do you mean "given that I offered it and it's a fair conclusion"? Let's be honest and let's be straight. Are they not there to protect Mladic as they must be there?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection to the form of the question. And of course if Mr. Karnavas is naturally leading the witness, that's what Mr. Butler was referring to previously. There's nothing dishonest about that. And the comments about "let's be honest," it's going to get worse and worse. It's not helpful.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It's less than accurate, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, your question, I believe, is quite argumentative. Please rephrase your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Are you suggesting, Mr. Butler, that there were no military police there guarding Mladic as they were required to do in Potocari on that day? Is that your answer?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. I am not meaning to suggest that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. So if the answer is no, then those -- there were military police from the Bratunac Brigade in Potocari as a result of a legal and necessary function.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I'm trying to do is just indicate that while that may be the purpose of the presence of some military police, I'm not going to say that that's the sole reason why they're there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. In the military police, we already indicated what the reserve, and they were not on that static line, that static defence line. Correct? So we can exclude them from my previous question.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Well I indicated -- never mind.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The military police --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Never mind.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- Were never engaged in -- they were never engaged to my knowledge therefore, they were never deployed in any of the battalion sectors, so yes, they weren't engaged in the defensive positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That's the point I was trying to make when I got the objection from the Prosecutor, so I'm breaking it down. You injected military police. So now we can conclude that some of those military police were there as a result of Mladic. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. There may have been others which we may or may not know why there were there. And then you indicated that there are several members of the Bratunac Brigade, several troops, and there we seem to have some disagreement as to whether they were there on orders or whether they were there on their own. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. In that respect, the disagreement is between the two witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, given -- in light of all of that, Colonel Blagojevic is not playing any role in Potocari on the 12th or the 13th, is he, with respect to these people that have gathered there? Some are bussed, and then some are screened, and then taken to Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Personally, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't believe -- well one or two people have identified him there. I don't offer that because I can't substantiate it. Certainly his units were involved in a number of the activities, and perhaps the best example is Major Trisic indicating that he was directed to bring food and bread in a continuing series of trucks down to Potocari. So in that respect, he was involved for the people.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And assuming he was involved, it sounds to me like that was a humanitarian and kind act as opposed to something nefarious and sinister?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, in that respect, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And again, just to make sure that I'm clear at least all of these years of your investigation, you cannot tell us who ordered these people, the ones that were screened and the ones that were bussed, put in buses and remained in Bratunac and those who were put into the facilities there, you don't know who made that order, who issued that order?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The obvious assumption is it would be General Mladic, but I don't know who specifically gave that order.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Well, let's move on, then. I think we can move on at this point. I want to talk a little bit about security because it has come up. And in fact, there was one particular piece of evidence that the Defence was able to locate thanks to the cooperation from -- the use of OTP's computer system where Ms. Tomanovic spent approximately 10 to 15 days going through the computer and found what I believe has been marked as P389. That's the instruction. If you can get it handy, we're not going to go to it right away, but just get it handy to you have it there ready to plop it up on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have it here in this pile, sir, so...

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We have an extra copy, sir. And while I'm at it, I can give you part of the transcript as well. The transcript will date to Tuesday 11 November 2003. I copied more than the relevant area for contextual purposes lest there be any problems and in case you wanted to refer to a particular section. Now, before we get to this exhibit, there was an issue or there was some discussion between you and the Prosecutor with respect to the term "counter-intelligence." Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: In fact, that was the point in time when I had stood up and requested if you could provide us a place, the source, that would give us an indication -- a definition of what "counter-intelligence" is. And in fact, the President made the same request as a result of my request. Then you were posed a question, and that's on page 4299 on line 22. And the question was: "So for counter-intelligence, Mr. Butler, we haven't gotten to the regulation yet, but there are definitions of counter-intelligence and discussions of counter-intelligence in those regulations, aren't there"? And the answer was: "Yes, sir, there are." And then there is another question and no reference as to which regulations, where specifically you had found a precise definition of counter-intelligence. So for the sake of clarity, do you know offhand where you have found a definition of counter-intelligence?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe the best source on that would be one of the documents that's an annex in my report or a footnote in my report. And it's called "The means and work of the intelligence and security services in the armed forces." I think it actually goes into the nuts and bolts or the tradecraft, even related issues with respect to that. So I think that would be the most appropriate starting place to come up with that definition.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And I take it that you could be -- you would be able to put your hand on it, not right now but at some point after we break today, put your hand on that piece of document and give it to the Registrar to copy so we could study it over the weekend? The definition now.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll try to find it. Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. In any event, let's get back to this document. Now, you were asked to give an analysis of the document. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And in fact, Mr. McCloskey went paragraph by paragraph and asked you to describe it and to analyse it and to give your reasoned and expert opinion. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And first, if we could go to the top of the second paragraph where it says: "With the aim of preventing..." If we could put this on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It's, for the record, P389.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'll just read. "With the aim of preventing these and similar problems in control of the security and intelligence organs and creating better conditions for their more effective use, I hereby issue the following instructions." Now, my question is: Is this instruction a control measure of a sort?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if we go to paragraph 2, and if we were to trace your testimony, which can be found on page 4311, if you could look at it -- do you have it? 4311.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Almost there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It begins on line 5. You can just look at it. You don't have to put it on the ELMO yet. And I think if you go to the following page at line 3, I think we will see that the entire question-and-answer process with respect to this paragraph is contained within these lines. Would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
