utterances.text: Yes, sir, I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And at some point, you commented, after the first paragraph of your answer, from line 11 to line 18 -- you can put this on the ELMO if you wish. I don't want to read it, but if you could look at it, and I will just give a general description of it. Basically what you do is analyse the first paragraph that's contained in paragraph number 2 of this instruction, P389. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And then there is a note by you where you have some problems with respect to, I believe, whether a law exists.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And just for the record, I thought it might help if you could look at P84. If I could have the kind assistance of Madam Usher. If you look at it, you will see it's just the relevant page from P84. It may require a number. In fact, I am told that it does. So this would be D84 for identification purposes. This is from the rules of service. Obviously you're acquainted with that, are you not? Rules of service of security organs?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If we turn the page and we go to page 30, go to paragraph 83, it would appear -- why don't we just read it for the record. It says: "In an imminent threat of war or mobilisation, security organs proceed according to the provisions of these rules, special instructions, internal mobilisation documents, mobilisation rules, rules of combat and other rules of regulations that regulate the work of these organs and the orders of competent military officers adapting their own activity, methods and means of work to the conditions of the mobilisation." Having read that, would it not appear that perhaps this instruction that we have here is the result of paragraph 83 of the rules of service?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, let me ask you this: Perhaps I'm misphrasing it. Would you agree with me based on what I just read that General Mladic had the authority to issue this instruction?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And would you agree with me that this instruction had to be complied with or by those beneath him?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, if we just look at your -- I couldn't help -- let me -- let me keep my thoughts out. If we look at your answer, one would conclude that you omitted in commenting about the second paragraph that's contained within paragraph 2. And let's read it and see what, if anything, we might be able to conclude. It says: "Furthermore, all members of these organs and services are authorised by law to act in work on tasks from their field of work analogous" - I underscore that a little bit, I emphasise it - "analogous to the authority of the members of the RS, the Republika Srpska, MUP, Ministry of the Interior, State Security Department." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, if you look at your answer, would you agree with me that you failed to comment about that aspect of paragraph 2 when you were given the opportunity to do so by the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, clearly it's missing. I'm not sure what the relevance is, but okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We're going to get to that. We're going to get to that slowly. It would appear at least from reading it that through this paragraph, the security branch now within the military is going to be treated analogous to the State Security Department of the Ministry of the Interior. Does it not appear that way?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't read it that way. I believe it basically says they are authorised to act by law -- or authorised by law to act and work on tasks from their field of work analogous to the authority of members of the RDB. Yes, sir. It's not a treatment issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Well, some would claim that what is contained in this paragraph is the beginning of creating an institution within an institution.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would disagree with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Do you know how the state security organ normally works?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have some very limited knowledge of it. I don't have a lot of the details of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. So you can't help us out at all on what might they be doing?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: My understanding of the State Security Department in this respect, we call it the RDB, is that they are primarily engaged in the collection of intelligence-related information, as we've indicated or as we've seen in the previous reports, exhibits, they're collecting intelligence. And I believe they also have the state counter-intelligence role and responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Secret police. Does that come in mind, that term?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That not a term I would use, but state security, not secret police.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. State security. I guess I'm trying to help you out. Aren't they really a police that is acting like a secret police? They're out there underground, more or less, doing clandestine work, collecting information. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: They're collecting information. They are doing clandestine work. I'm just not making the next jump to secret police.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Let me ask you this: Did the security organ or -- did the State Security Department in the former Yugoslavia have any particular sort of a reputation?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And was that one that would conjure up any particular image or vision that comes to your mind at this point?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. The former -- they would probably qualify as your definition of the -- what is it? The secret police.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And was that benevolent society of police officers?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I guess that entirely depends on whether you're holding the leash or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. But for the ordinary citizen, who would that conjure up?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would conjure up fear.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And so now we have -- the security organ is to be accorded the same authority and act analogous to the State Security Department within this military institution. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what the document says, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. So that's why I asked you does not this paragraph give us the impression that Mladic himself is trying to create an institution within an institution?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, the reason why I disagree is because to my knowledge, the Republika Srpska RDB did not function as a secret police. I mean, I think by your own definition the fact that the secret police were so feared, when the SDS created their own party and then subsequently the state evolved around it, nobody wanted an institution like that which would birddog them. So again, I have no evidence that the RDB functions like that, and because I don't I can't make the conclusion that the military is going to function as a gestapo.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Just as an aside, since you're with the Prosecutor's Office, do you know if they are trying to tie in the State Security Department of Serbia in the Milosevic case as being involved in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: From 1992 to 1995?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay, thanks. Now, if we go on to paragraph 3, now incidentally, before we get there, was there any particular reason why you chose to totally ignore commenting on this, not even giving us an aside?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. That is a misstatement of the facts. There's no indication he totally ignored anything. And it's just argumentative.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Karnavas, put your question another way.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I will, Your Honour. I will.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Is there any particular reason why you failed to note about this particular paragraph when you were directly asked by the Prosecutor with whom I assume that I sat down and analysed this and talked about what this document might mean, why it is that this portion of paragraph 2 was so -- was left out of your commentary?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, sir, again, I didn't -- the same reason before, I didn't think it was relevant. And since I didn't attribute the same meaning to the RS RDB as you did, it isn't relevant. Strictly in my mind they have the same rights and privileges with respect to their duties. I now see that given the slant that you put on it where it would be relevant, and I assume that's why we're bringing it up. But for my direct testimony, I don't see it as relevant.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. The slant, might that be it's helpful to my client, Colonel Blagojevic, and it's against the Prosecution? Might that slant being my slant, that it doesn't really help your case?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. The slant that I'm referring to is that, you know, your affiliation with -- of the RDB in the same vein as a secret police organisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right, all right. Now, we go to paragraph 3. And if we flip the page, and if you could assist us with the ELMO, too. Page 4312. This is rather short. It would appear that -- the question is on line 3. And you devote approximately four lines to this, perhaps five. And so maybe we can read along. Line -- you're asked a question on line 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: In paragraph 3, what is that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Paragraph 3 sets the framework that obligates all members of the armed forces, the VRS in this case, VRS institution commands and other members to provide assistance to the organs in the realisation of their intelligence and security tasks and to not take any actions which could endanger those type of tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. What else in this document do you find of significance? And then you go to paragraph 4. Do you recall giving us that answer, having been posed that question by Mr. McCloskey back on 11 November 2003? Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, I want you to please focus your attention to the second paragraph within paragraph number 3. We can put that on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's on the ELMO, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Thank you for anticipating the situation here on the ground. It says: "At the same time" - at the same time - "to the extent and in the measure necessary, members of the security and intelligence organs must provide their immediate superiors with information, assessments, and observations regarding the security of units or institutions." Question: Would you agree with me that in your explanation of paragraph 3, you failed to comment on this particular portion of paragraph number 3?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, it's not in there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It's not in there because you failed to comment on it. Right?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, let's go step by step. It seems to be a little bit of a discussion regarding reciprocity here. If we go back to the first portion of the paragraph on the first page it, starts with: "It is the obligation of all VRS..." In other words, no discretion. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. "Shall," "must." Would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. If we turn to the next paragraph, and this is where it is rather interesting, it doesn't start with "it is the obligation" or "at the same time it is the obligation." But rather says: "At the same time, to the extent and in the measures necessary," and from this can we not conclude that here it is up to the security organ and that -- the security and intelligence organs to determine what extent and when necessary?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. That is a function of the security officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: In other words, they have the discretion to choose when it is they are going to provide their immediate superiors with information, assessments, and observations regarding the security of units or institutions. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't quite read it like that. I read it more on the lines of that they are expected when they receive information or intelligence, that they provide that -- that are relevant to their superiors, that they provide it. When they receive information that is not relevant, that that's not information that has to be provided. I don't -- it's not an optional issue. I believe it is -- again, assuming the security officers work within the confines of, you know, their -- the rules and regulations, there are certain pieces of information that wouldn't be going to the commander and the superior and that the security officer would retain for himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Let me just break it down so we can all understand that answer. You say "relevant," "when it's relevant." What do you mean by "relevant"?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: For example, when an intelligence or security officer, based on a prisoner-of-war interrogation, gets information about enemy troop units or locations or intentions, that is a piece of information that I believe would be something that would be relevant and would be a piece of information passed to the commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And who determines what is and is not relevant?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Under these rules and regulations, that is under the purview of the security officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And since they hold the key to that vault, it would be only when they decided what is or is not relevant that -- that the immediate superior would be informed. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, with respect to immediate superior, in this particular case or this contextual case, I take the immediate superior to be the commander. Under the same regulations, they will always be informing their immediate superior within the functional chain.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you. That was my next -- that was my very next question. So that in other words what you're saying to us, to put it in an example form, Nikolic would decide what is relevant for his immediate commander, Colonel Blagojevic, is to know. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But he would inform or there would be that functional command between Nikolic and Popovic, Nikolic and Beara, and so on. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The chain would run from Nikolic to Popovic. And again it's done so with the respect to functional command, Popovic would receive the same information and arguably he may decide that despite a subordinate's judgement, that this is something that needs to go around to other people.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You're right.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: So that is why the system is designed as it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And it could be the converse. See, I'm trying to get you to give us the other side. And conversely, they could say this is the kind of information we do not want you to share with your superior. Right?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: With respect to the work and means of the branch, there is information that is not shared, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: See, I want to pin you down because when it hurts me, you have no problem. And I'm trying to get you to acknowledge that in cases --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We're getting into all these personal feelings. We're getting into wrestling terminology. This is argumentative.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour. I'll rephrase.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'll rephrase. Heart be still.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Would you acknowledge, in just a very direct way, that it could work just the other way as well? Beara could tell Popovic not to share this information with Krstic, and Popovic could tell Nikolic "don't share this information with Blagojevic"? Isn't that just -- doesn't it work that way as well?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. And I believe that I tendered an exhibit which showed just that happening.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Okay, well, I wanted to be clear on this matter. Now, just, again, I'm trying to figure this one out. Is there any reason why you didn't volunteer this information when you were given an opportunity to comment on paragraph 3? Albeit it does affect the Defence in a positive way.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe -- I don't believe that it's a question of that. It just reflects material that is already listed in the JNA security regulations.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't believe there was anything wrong by omission. The document was on the ELMO for everyone to see.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But you were asked to comment on it, sir. You were asked to give us your analysis. You have come here as the analyst who analysed and synthesised. And all I'm trying to point out here is here's another example where perhaps your analysis could have been of some assistance. And yet, you deprived us of that assistance. And now I'm prying it out of you. Would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I mean, how much is enough? Prying it out of him. Pinning him down. I could go on and on. It's absurd.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Paragraph --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: -- It's really argumentative. Try to ask a very simple question. I know your point. Try to ask --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm sugar-coating this, by the way, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I don't think it's sugar-coating.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Let's go on to paragraph 4. Now, on paragraph number 4, on the second, the second paragraph, in the second sentence in the paragraph, it says: "The manner in and extent to which the commander or other organs of the command shall be informed about the contents of these telegrams or mail shall be regulated exclusively by the appropriate security and intelligence organs." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, I just want to -- you did comment on this. And I want to commend you, first of all. And secondly, you said, on the next page -- on page 4313, you use the term "need to know" -- "on a basis of need to know." That was your term. Do you see that? On page 4313, line 1. "Need to know."

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And that sort of in that nice little catchy phrase encapsulates the essence of paragraph 4. In other words, the security organ is going to decide on its own the extent to which their immediate commander, the immediate superior, is going to be provided with information.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, with respect to the tasks on the -- in the instruction, yes. It dovetails that the Main Staff is where you have the coalescence between the operative and command and the security branch. So while it goes up the security channel, it doesn't hit the operator; it hits at the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. So in other words, to put it bluntly, Nikolic decides what his immediate superior, that is, Colonel Blagojevic, needs to know.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: With respect to the functions in this instruction, yes, sir, he does.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Or he recommends it at least to his superior Popovic if he doesn't have the authority himself to release it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. So when he's working with Popovic and when he's working with Kosoric, because this also seems to reflect intelligence as well, and when he's working with Beara, it would seem, would it not, that unless instructed otherwise by Popovic, Kosoric, or Beara, the sole discretion on what his superior Colonel Blagojevic will know will be left up to him. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: With relation to these tasks, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And a lot of these tasks on a need-to-know basis come under the umbrella of what is commonly referred to as "counter-intelligence." Correct? That's one of the times when they have that discretionary power?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And counter-intelligence, would you not agree with me, and you did provide us with a description of it, but counter-intelligence, it's more like you know it when you see it, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Actually, the process of counter-intelligence is fairly well regulated within the context of the JNA rules and regulations in that respect.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The problem is, Mr. Butler --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The information you may know it when you see it, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'd just like to say that I don't know that that's the best phrase that I would use, "you know it when you see it".

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. But if, for instance, I was the security officer, the assistant commander for security and intelligence or the head of security and intelligence. I don't know if he was actually wore that title because it was a light infantry brigade. I would determine what would be -- what would constitute counter-intelligence.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, the security officer would do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And in fact, if his commander would say to me, Karnavas, what are you up to? I could say: "I'm involved in counter-intelligence. You know better than that." That would be enough for my commander to walk away. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. I mean, if he had informed him of that and Colonel Blagojevic or any other commander would understand that if you wanted to know what he was doing at that point, you didn't have a right to, so to speak, badger that officer, but you had the right to go to his superior. And you may or may not get the same answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And that's assuming -- that's assuming that I would go to my commanding officer because I don't need permission or I'm not required to inform my immediate superior that I'm engaged in whatever I believe to be counter-intelligence activity. Correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Could we get the rank of the soldier Karnavas in this hypothetical.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I indicated that I'm the head of security and intelligence. I'm the assistant commander.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: In a brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I understand. But this question is quite hypothetical. Unless it's related to a specific case in our present sitting, otherwise, you know, it's very difficult for us to --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I will use Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I understand he's within our facilities here today.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Nikolic was the chief of security and intelligence for the Bratunac Brigade. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, he would not need to inform his commander that he's engaged in counter-intelligence; hence, he was going to go off and do whatever was necessary for his tasks. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, his commander may know that he's involved in counter-intelligence-related tasks. But under these instructions and the broader regulations, the commander has no right to inquire as to the specifics.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And there's no obligation - that's what I want to get to - that there's no obligation on Nikolic to inform him commander. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: With respect to the specifics, you're right, sir, there's no obligation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: In fact, it would be contrary to the whole concept of counter-intelligence; the whole point of it is to keep it a secret. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So you're not going to tell your commander, "I'm involved in secret counter-intelligence activity. You're not supposed to know, but just so you know, that's what I'm doing." That defeats the entire purpose. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. And that's not something that you would expect to see.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I know that I'm almost out of time. I think I have about a minute. Just out of curiosity, in reading Nikolic's statement, we see, and I think I pounded this point fairly hard, that he wasn't, on the 6th, 7th, 8th, 9th, 10th, and 11th, he had absolutely no contact with his commander who was at Pribicevac while he was back in the headquarters of Bratunac Brigade. Did that cause you any discomfort as to -- maybe not discomfort, but did that cause you any curiosity as to why this particular officer, the head of security and intelligence during the most important military campaign of that particular brigade and perhaps of the Drina Corps during that period of time was nowhere to be seen and had no contact with his commander? Did that cause you any concern?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, I believe it's quite unlikely that he didn't during that period. I would be very surprised if ultimately it turns out that during that six-day period he had no contact with his commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Assuming, assuming that he told us on that occasion the truth - in other words, that he had no contact - could we not conclude based on your military experience and your reading of the rules that here we are dealing with an individual who does whatever he pleases, particularly because of his position as being the chief of security and intelligence? Can we draw that conclusion, sir?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that he does whatever he wants. While I understand that in interviews with other officers of the brigade, they may acknowledge that he is engaged in activities that they're not aware. I don't take that as whoever he wants. He is still part of, by regulation and by this instruction, a member of the commander's inner circle, and he still has to report his activities at least to the superior security officer. So I wouldn't go as far as he does whatever he wants. But he does have a certain amount of latitude.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And that would mean being absent for all that period of time? That doesn't bother you at all?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, as I noted, if that turns out to be -- I don't think that that's the case. I would find it very unrealistic that he would be absent or not in contact with his commander during those critical days. That would surprise me very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, that were his testimony, then he must have committed perjury on that one as well. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, objection. This is -- the Court can come to its own conclusion on these sorts of issues. And I think it's readily clear --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I have no more questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: -- and I don't think he testified that he was absent, so it's full of nonsense.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I think I made my point, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I think I made the point quite well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: So we'll break now, and we'll resume, as I said, Monday 9.00 in Courtroom II.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 24th day of November, 2003, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.50 p.m.,
